firms.source: NASA GIBS FIRMS thermal anomaly layers (2023-08-08), rasterised
firms.note: n counts rendered marker pixels on a 0.005-deg grid, not individual detections

result.caveats: FIRMS clusters at Kilauea summit (1 km, n=45) and Mauna Loa summit (17 km, n=21) are likely volcanic heat, not wildfires, confounding distance metrics for plume 1. No SO2, AOD, or eruption-rate data available; classification uses only true-color morphology, geometry, fire distance and 10-m reanalysis wind. Plume 1 upwind gap and weak local summit wind make origin ambiguous and could be mixed vog plus transported wildfire smoke.
evidence: dominant plume 1 is largest (17710 km2, 279 km, clear) broad diffuse pale gray veil W-SW of Hawaii Island, not thin bluish-gray vent-trailing vog
plume 1 upwind end 69.1 km from Mauna Loa summit and 85.7 km from Kilauea summit, offset SW, not at active vent
plume 1 nearest non-summit fire is Kailua-Kona clusters >90-122 km away; nearest clusters are summit thermal anomalies themselves
plume 2 and 3 show clear wildfire-smoke geometry but are smaller/fainter than plume 1, so overall dominant haze cannot be confidently assigned
